symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of a length-W output vector, a power of two greater than q.
symbols.quote: Here $W$ denotes the target length, a count of entries that is a power of two greater than $q$; this letter changes meaning here.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The width of the Gaussian weights, an integer at least 2 with sigma squared less than p.
symbols.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the Gaussian width, an integer with $2\le\sigma$ and $\sigma^2<p$, where $p>100$ is the precision; this letter changes meaning here.

symbols.name: output index
symbols.meaning: The index of an entry of a length-W output vector, running from 0 to W minus 1.
symbols.quote: For a length-$q$ vector $u$ with entries $u_j$ ($0\le j<q$, indices read modulo $q$) and an output index $k$ with $0\le k<W$ (this letter changes meaning here), let $\Psi$ and $\Xi$ be the maps defined by the weighted sums below, where $\Psi$ gathers the inputs $j$ near $qk/W$ and $\Xi$ spreads entry $j$ over the outputs $k$ near $Wj/q$:

symbols.name: first Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The first Gaussian-weighted sum, mapping a length-q vector to a length-W vector.
symbols.quote: For a length-$q$ vector $u$ with entries $u_j$ ($0\le j<q$, indices read modulo $q$) and an output index $k$ with $0\le k<W$ (this letter changes meaning here), let $\Psi$ and $\Xi$ be the maps defined by the weighted sums below, where $\Psi$ gathers the inputs $j$ near $qk/W$ and $\Xi$ spreads entry $j$ over the outputs $k$ near $Wj/q$:

symbols.name: second Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The second Gaussian-weighted sum, mapping a length-q vector to a length-W vector.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The selection map taking, for each j below q, the entry of a length-W vector at the integer nearest Wj/q.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal J$ take, for $0\le j<q$, entry $\lfloor Wj/q+\tfrac12\rfloor$ of a length-$W$ vector, the integer nearest $Wj/q$ with ties upward.

symbols.name: diagonal correction
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying entry j of a length-q vector by the factor that cancels the weight of Xi at the selected output.
symbols.quote: Let $\Upsilon$ multiply entry $j$ by $\exp\big(\pi\sigma^2(Wj/q-\lfloor Wj/q+\tfrac12\rfloor)^2\big)$, which cancels the weight of $\Xi$ at the selected output.

symbols.name: middle map
symbols.meaning: The length-q map J Xi Upsilon, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Set $\mathcal N=\mathcal J\,\Xi\,\Upsilon$, a map from length $q$ to length $q$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-q vectors that moves entry Wj mod q to position j.
symbols.quote: Let $\Pi_q$ and $\Pi_W$ be the coordinate permutations $(\Pi_q u)_j=u_{Wj \bmod q}$ and $(\Pi_W u)_k=u_{-qk \bmod W}$.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-W vectors that moves entry minus qk mod W to position k.
symbols.quote: Let $\Pi_q$ and $\Pi_W$ be the coordinate permutations $(\Pi_q u)_j=u_{Wj \bmod q}$ and $(\Pi_W u)_k=u_{-qk \bmod W}$.

symbols.name: input contraction
symbols.meaning: The map Psi divided by 2, a contraction from length q to length W.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length $q$ by a transform of power-of-two length, so that the later steps can use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.
It reshapes the transforms of the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) that the integer product needs.
Gaussian resampling replaces the Fourier transforms by [multidimensional transforms](multidimensional-transform.md) whose axis lengths are powers of two.
Gaussian resampling converts the lengths for the [synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md) into powers of two.
Gaussian resampling requires its lengths to be [coprime](coprime.md), $\gcd(q,W)=1$.
Gaussian resampling measures contraction with the [array norm](array-norm.md).
